A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Content can be matched reliably across the added supplementary section, table renumbering, and page shifts.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA benchmark experiments, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and supplementary Env-QA results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds human evaluation of rewritten questions, an overall inference-time comparison, and another grounding-ablation control.

M1.justification: The entailment construction, verification, scoring, pruning, answer selection, and appendix prompts are retained. Newly specified grounding intervals document implementation rather than establish an algorithm change; their inconsistent direction labels are a documentation issue.

E1.justification: Both versions cover NExT-QA, IntentQA, short-video VideoMME, Env-QA, and NExT-GQA grounding annotations. The added human and timing studies reuse NExT-QA and its existing question-answering requirements; video-free answering was already illustrated in Figure 4.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds a comparison configuration with neither fact-conditioned captioning nor structure-based retrieval enabled. The named external baselines remain unchanged, and the new timing comparison reuses previously evaluated methods.

E3.justification: The new human study randomly samples 1,000 original and 1,000 rewritten questions for four volunteers, with and without video. Table 15 introduces per-video timing and specifies 16 uniformly sampled 224-by-224 frames for VideoChat2 and VideoLLaVA. These are added protocols, not demonstrated changes to the retained benchmark experiments.

E4.justification: v2 materially broadens validation through direct human assessment of rewritten-question answerability and textual shortcuts (Section 8, Table 9), plus an overall accuracy-runtime analysis (Table 15). It also completes the grounding-component ablation with a neither-component control. Earlier component studies and qualitative examples remain.

E5.justification: Both versions use point estimates without reported model-run variability, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 9 specifies averaging accuracy across four volunteers, but does not introduce uncertainty estimation; the participant count belongs to the new study design.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores are retained. New results include the Table 5 control at 56.2/49.6 accuracy, human accuracy of 96.4/93.9 with video and 79.3/44.6 without video on original/rewritten questions, and Table 15's 38.2-second inference time with 62.6 accuracy for the proposed framework. These are additional measurements, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The decomposition condition, confidence calculations, pruning criterion, and backtracking rule are unchanged. Equation 4's direct-score notation and accompanying grounded-moment description are clarified, without new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about video-grounded entailment reasoning, de-biased evaluation, and competitive performance remain. v2 foregrounds a 257-fold reasoner parameter comparison, but v1 already makes the approximately 250-fold comparison in its supplement; this mainly changes emphasis.

C2.justification: The added overall efficiency discussion interprets runtime and reasoner size as evidence of practical competitiveness, extending v1's focus on dynamic-tree call savings. The human-study discussion also explicitly relates retained answerability and reduced text-only accuracy to benchmark fairness.

D1.justification: v2 specifies grounding-window boundaries and an eight-frame look-around interval, states that the framework requires no training or human annotation, and documents timing settings. It removes the promised code release upon acceptance. The new look-ahead boundary conflicts with Figure 2's after-event example, limiting the clarification.

R1.justification: Four references are added concerning invariant grounding, task-adaptive video sampling, few-shot action recognition, and dense video captioning. Their inclusion modestly expands contextual citations without substantially changing the positioning relative to entailment-tree and VQA methods.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar, terminology, and explanatory edits, rewrites the conclusion, and inserts a supplementary quality-assessment section. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact; later supplementary sections are renumbered.

P2.justification: v2 adds human-evaluation and efficiency tables, expands Table 5, relocates Tables 7–8, and adjusts captions and title layout. Existing supplementary tables are renumbered. The five appendix pages containing Figures 6–14 are visually identical after their page shift.

improvement.justification: The human study provides useful direct support for rewritten-question answerability and reduced textual shortcuts, while the added control and runtime comparison strengthen validation and practical assessment. These gains leave the core results unchanged. The inconsistent grounding-direction documentation and removal of the code-release commitment temper the improvement.
